text:
Montreal woke up to the news it has chased for months. Daily Faceoff posted "Canadiens acquire Dylan Larkin from Red Wings" on Monday, and The Athletic's Shayna Goldman wrote that "the Dylan Larkin saga has finally ended." Larkin's trade request had hung over Detroit all season. Whether he dresses tonight against Los Angeles is unknown, and nothing here counts him: our projections were built before the deal.

The Canadiens he joins have been winning on more than their chances. They have 32 points against 24.8 our numbers say they deserved, at 51% of the five-on-five expected goals (expected goals measure the quality of chances). The difference has mostly been Jacob Fowler: .918 and 12.4 goals saved above expected in 15 games, enough for Daily Faceoff to call him the easy Calder favorite. Saturday stung anyway: Noah Cates scored with 31 seconds left and Montreal fell 4-3 to the Flyers, a night the coverage hung on a costly Fowler mistake. The injury list is long: Ivan Demidov (ankle), Chris Kreider (out until about January), Mike Matheson and Josh Anderson. Juraj Slafkovský has gone 15 games without a goal on 5.0 expected, which is a drought, not a collapse.

The Kings are the mirror image. Their goal difference is -13 on +1.7 expected, with finishing and Darcy Kuemper (.885, 5.2 goals below expected) both costing them, and our numbers give them a 28% playoff chance. Help may be close: Artemi Panarin and Trevor Moore are off the out list and day-to-day. Drew Doughty plays his 1,300th game, on a week when Daily Faceoff asked whether the Kings could sell him. Corey Perry, a fourth-liner with 3.3 expected goals in his last ten, is one of our Sleepers.

We have Montreal at 3.48 expected goals and Los Angeles at 2.94. Watch Fowler's response to Saturday, and watch Nick Suzuki, at 71% for a point, with a new center in the building.
headline: Larkin news lands on a Canadiens game night
